steps.caption: For small nonprofits and food banks. This is the deployed AWS app with fictional volunteers and shifts.
Pantry preparation needs one volunteer. Kind checks availability, qualifications, conflicts, opt in and contact limits.
We choose Strands + Amazon Bedrock. This run uses the real Nova Lite model, with three bounded tools.
Strands prepared a draft. The agent cannot approve the invitation, send a message or assign a volunteer.
The coordinator can edit the exact invitation. Only their approval activates the response link.
Approval creates a scoped response page. This demo does not send email or SMS; the link can be shared manually.
The volunteer sees their invitation and shift, then accepts or declines. They do not get the full roster.
Acceptance checks eligibility and remaining capacity again, then saves the assignment. Repeat responses cannot overfill it.
The coordinator now sees the shift covered. The roster and activity persist in DynamoDB across sessions.
Saved preparation history shows the real tool activity. Model preparation stays separate from approval and acceptance.
Judges can restart the fictional sample for future shifts. Confirmation explains the reset; the daily AI allowance is preserved.

recording: Actual deployed UI with editorial caption overlays and title cards. No narration audio. A confirmed API sample restart created fresh data before recording. The UI confirmation was later opened and cancelled.
